_comment: Accepted codegen-differential defects, per (component, attribute, platform, check). An entry means the converter demonstrably fails that judgement and the failure is accepted FOR A STATED REASON — not that it is fine. Unrecorded defects fail `jui conformance gate --codegen-effect`; entries the measurement no longer supports are stale and fail too, so fixing a defect forces its row out (the one-directional version lets a fixed row sit here forever, which is how the previous freeze ledgers rotted). Advisory classes (value-is-default, numeric-string-divergence) are re-derived every run and are deliberately absent. Reason 'unreviewed-initial-measurement' marks the initial-measurement backlog — consume it.

entries.owner: E (SSoT) — contract, no implementation is owed on this face
entries.reason: Contract, not a gap. The collectionSeparators ruling (2026-08-07, raised by B) settles it: the ios probe path is CollectionStackView, not SwiftUI's List, and a container that draws no separators satisfies 'hide the separators' VACUOUSLY. 'Implement it' must not mean 'switch the container to a List' — an attribute that reshapes the thing it modifies is the defect family this wave exists to remove. The coverage row is runtime-only: the ios DYNAMIC path implements it; no codegen face does, by contract.

entries.owner: D (fixture shape) — the List-path implementation landed in sjui ba5e6d1
entries.reason: NOT unread: sjui collection_converter.rb reads the declared vocabulary and emits `.listStyle(PlainListStyle/GroupedListStyle/InsetGroupedListStyle/SidebarListStyle)`, enumerated by the collectionSeparators ruling (2026-08-07). The probe cannot reach that line: its layout carries `sections`, which routes to CollectionStackView — a container that is NOT a SwiftUI List and therefore has no list chrome to pick. The ruling states the measurement consequence up front: 'the fixture must use a list-shaped Collection to observe this at all', and it forbids the other reading — an attribute must not reshape the container it modifies. The row leaves this ledger when the probe stands on a list-shaped Collection.

entries.owner: D (fixture shape) — the converter is correct
entries.reason: Structurally unreachable in the probe's layout, and the converter is right. image_converter.rb reads it as `if src … elsif defaultImage || errorImage || loadingImage …` — a FALLBACK, which by its own declaration applies only when no src resolves. The probe writes `src` AND `defaultImage` on the same node, so the fallback arm is dead by construction and no value of the attribute could change the emit. Same shape as the Image/src measurement blind spot already recorded elsewhere. The row leaves this ledger when the probe drops `src` from the base for this attribute.

entries.owner: A (rjui) — probe value fix owned by D
entries.reason: NOT an unread spelling. collection_converter.rb:149-151 reads it and every container branch acts on it: static `none` drops the overflow scroll classes (measured: CONTROL/lazy/eager byte-identical, none differs), and the bound form emits a runtime overflow override in all three branches. The C0 verdict is an artifact of the value plan: representative_value('Collection','lazy') is 'lazy' — the declared DEFAULT — so emit(v1) equals the control by construction, and the second value 'eager' also equals it because lazy-vs-eager is virtualization, which the plain `.map()` emit does not have. `none` is the only web-observable value and the probe never picks it.
entries.note: Accepted degeneracy: web lazy≡eager (no virtualization to switch off). Probe fix: representative value `none` in rules.py (D's file, not touched here).
